added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no base gate log, so the added-failure count was not taken

findings.text: follow-on: the retained refusal branch at review.py:1987 is unreachable for any id in the standard run-id grammar, because the guard on `if encoded:` at review.py:1984 returns RUN_ID_TIMES_SOURCE first and every minted id encodes a dispatch instant. So a review run whose own record exists but carries no dispatch stamp is committed under times_source run-id rather than refused, contradicting the resolve_record_times docstring (review.py:2005-2009) and the store_committed_review docstring, which both state such a record is refused naming the run; the branch carries no test (the refusal case was replaced, not augmented), so nothing shows it fires.

follow-on: the reviewed manifest names its gate log only under test_logs and records no baseline_suite/after_suite suite fields, so the store's annotate_review_of_run derives no added-failure count for this run; the one-arm evidence cannot distinguish a change that added no failing test from one whose base arm was never taken. Recording the arm logs under the manifest's suite fields would let a later reader derive the delta.

item_verdicts.done_when: the three-file gate ran 29 passed EXIT=0 (independent re-run at 8948df23); the refusal case was replaced by test_a_record_resolving_no_time_is_committed_marked_unknown and test_a_record_with_resolvable_times_keeps_them added; the reviewed manifest records the negative control red (1 failed EXIT=1).
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is exactly delivered; see the goal_fidelity justification.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; the head arm reads 29 passed EXIT=0 and the negative control 1 failed EXIT=1, but the manifest names its gate log under test_logs rather than the after_suite field the store reads and records no baseline_suite, so the store's added-failure derivation reads unmeasured.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the diff touches exactly review.py, the test file and the evidence fragment, all inside the declared scope.

justifications.durability: test_a_record_resolving_no_time_is_committed_marked_unknown pins the new unknown branch and test_a_record_with_resolvable_times_keeps_them pins that the run-id path is unchanged, and the negative control reddens the former. But the retained refusal branch (own_run_record_found, review.py:1987) carries no test and is unreachable for any id in the run-id grammar, so the defect it claims to catch is never refused in production.
justifications.evidence: The declared gate (three test files) ran to its summary line at head: I re-ran it at 8948df23, 29 passed EXIT=0; the reviewed manifest records the negative control red (1 failed, 28 passed, EXIT=1) and I read that log, which shows the restored refusal reddening test_a_record_resolving_no_time_is_committed_marked_unknown. The reviewed manifest names no baseline_suite/after_suite gate logs, so the added-failure count is not derivable and is recorded unmeasured (null), not a measured zero.
justifications.fit: The added names describe mechanism — UNKNOWN_TIMES_SOURCE, _run_record_times_found — with no version, plan or ticket identifier and no attribution, and the docstrings explain the two branches. The resolve_record_times docstring (review.py:2005-2009) overstates the refusal's reach, claiming a run whose record exists but carries no dispatch stamp is refused, which the code does not do when the id encodes an instant.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The stated goal is delivered and reproduced: a record whose review run has no record anywhere and whose id encodes no instant is committed rather than refused — store_committed_review now reaches resolve_record_times's new fall-through (review.py:2004) and stores empty dispatched_at/completed_at with times_source unknown (UNKNOWN_TIMES_SOURCE, review.py:1258), never the store timestamp; I re-ran the gate at 8948df23 and read the assertions that pin empty stamps, source unknown, and timestamp distinct from both stamps.
justifications.reuse: run_record_times keeps its public, documented 2-tuple signature as a thin wrapper over the new private _run_record_times_found (review.py:1800), which the public function and resolve_record_times share, so the pointer/ledger lookup is written once and the found flag is added without a second reader of the run record, and no existing caller changes.
justifications.scope_discipline: The diffstat over 5f53ef9d..8948df23 lists exactly reckon/crew/review.py, tests/test_review_store_owns_identity_and_times.py and the evidence fragment docs/evidence/fragments/every-review-is-kept-as-a-committed-record/a-review-without-times-is-still-kept.html — all inside the node's declared write paths; the declared figures directory was not created because the done-when names no artifact.
